newsitem.title: FRANCE: Junior French minister resigns after by-election.
newsitem.headline: Junior French minister resigns after by-election.

text.p: Margie Sudre, a junior French foreign minister, said she was resigning on Sunday after losing a by-election on the Indian Ocean island of La Reunion.

Sudre, secretary of state for Francophonie, the club of French-speaking countries grouping 400 million people worldwide, was beaten by Communist Claude Hoarau in a run-off vote for election to the National Assembly.
"This evening I am handing back the La Francophonie portfolio to the Prime Minister and the President," she said in a radio interview. She won won 44 percent of the vote to 56 percent for Hoarau.
"We have lost a battle, we have not lost the war," she said.
Sudre, with backing from Prime Minister Alain Juppe and other members of the centre-right cabinet, had urged massive turnout in Sunday's vote in a traditional Communist constituency.
After the first round open to all candidates a week ago, Hoarau was ahead with 47.6 percent to 42.5 percent for Sudre. Neither won half the vote, forcing the run-off.
The seat fell vacant because Communist Paul Verges shifted to the Senate. It was Sudre's first attempt to win election to the National Assembly.

Sudre won regional elections in 1993 at the head of the so-called "Freedom" list, born of calls for liberalisation of audiviosual rules for La Reunion. She has appointed when Juppe became prime minister in 1995.
Among her projects has been to challenge the domination of English on the Internet world computer network.
